newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi jail inmates riot, sheriff blames overcrowding.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi jail inmates riot, sheriff blames overcrowding.

text.p: Two dozen inmates rioted at the Adams County Jail on Wednesday, barricading themselves on the second floor and demanding a meeting with the governor, authorities said.

Police said the inmates refused to return to their cells after lunch Wednesday and barricaded themselves behind mattresses and large metal tables. They had not been subdued by 10:30 p.m. CDT, authorities said.
WLBT-TV in Jackson, Miss., reported Sheriff Tommy Ferrell said there were no hostages and no information was available on injuries. He also blamed the incident on overcrowding.
Deputies said the inmates were demanding television sets, telephones and press coverage of their complaints, as well as a meeting with Gov. Kirk Fordice.
Mississippi Highway Patrol tactical teams were at the jail in full riot gear. Deputies would not says if the inmates were armed and Ferrell could not be reached for comment.
